findings.situation: A filer paid $1,700 of medical expenses in 2024 but could deduct only $200 because of the medical-expense floor, then received a $500 insurance reimbursement in 2025. Answering truthfully, the filer enters $500, and that full amount flows uncapped to Worksheet 2, line 2.
findings.source_text: p525 p. 27, Worksheet 2 footnote 2: "Don't enter more than the amount deducted for the prior year"; p525 p. 26, Example 34: "The only amount of the $500 reimbursement that must be included in your income for 2025 is $200, the amount actually deducted."
findings.why: The question 'How much of the medical and dental bills you paid in 2024 was repaid to you … in 2025?' asks for the gross reimbursement. Line 2 needs that amount limited to the medical deduction actually taken for 2024, and no line between the answer and line 2 applies that cap.

locators: p. 26, Example 34, "In 2025, you received a $500 reimbursement from your medical insurance for your 2024 expenses"
p. 27, Worksheet 2, line 2, "Enter the total of all other Schedule A (Form 1040) refunds or reimbursements"
